item.content:encoded:
News / Benzinga / The Musk Midterms Trade: SPCX Flat, TSLA Drops 5% but DOGE Plunges 7%

The Musk Midterms Trade: SPCX Flat, TSLA Drops 5% but DOGE Plunges 7% 1 min read

DOGEUSD SPCX TSLA ETHUSD Dogecoin DOGEUSD is down 7% since the midterms, trailing both SpaceX SPCX and Tesla TSLA even though all three are tied to Elon Musk . Musk’s Three Assets Diverge After Election Day From the Nov. 3 close through Nov. 9, SpaceX gained 0.50%, Tesla fell 5%, and Dogecoin dropped 7%, according to official sources. The selloff deepened Nov. 5, when Tesla and SpaceX shed roughly $456 billion combined, with SpaceX down 9% and Tesla down 12% on fears a Democratic Congress could slow their AI data center buildout and a rumored merger. SpaceX then rebounded nearly 15% through Nov. 9, erasing its losses entirely, while Tesla recovered 10% but stayed below its pre-election level. However, Dogecoin never turned the corner. Analysts Split Tesla and SpaceX’s Political Risk As Benzinga reported, a Bitunix analyst argued Tesla and SpaceX face different political risks following Texas Democrat Gina Hinojosa’s midterm win, with expansion plans, not existing operations, representing the real concern. That distinction may help explain why investors treated the two Musk companies differently once the initial selloff passed. SpaceX’s own earnings gave investors an additional reason to look past the political overhang. Benzinga reported the company posted third-quarter revenue of $14.58 billion, beating the $12.74 billion analysts expected, with earnings of 35 cents per share against estimates of 12 cents. Revenue climbed 161% year over year, fueled by SpaceX’s Super Intelligence segment. Why Dogecoin Never Found Its Own Catalyst Dogecoin had no earnings report, merger speculation or AI revenue story to anchor a recovery, leaving it exposed to broader crypto weakness instead. As Benzinga reported this week, October CPI came in hotter than expected, pushing December Fed rate hike odds toward 77% and dragging Bitcoin, Ethereum ETHUSD and XRP XRPUSD lower alongside Dogecoin, pressure that compounded lingering fallout from the Binance hack still rattling crypto sentiment heading into the election. item.content:encoded:
News / GuruFocus / NVIDIA Stocks Slide 4.43% as Report Alleges $7.5 Billion in Chips Reached China

NVIDIA Stocks Slide 4.43% as Report Alleges $7.5 Billion in Chips Reached China 1 min read

NVDA NVIDIA NVDA shares fell 4.43% to $170.75 as of 9:53 a.m. ET in regular trading on November 10, after The Information reported that Jensen Huang's personal relationship with a businesswoman alleged to work for Beijing helped move at least $7.5 billion of its chips to Chinese firms. That stacks on Monday's 4.27% drop. Reuters, which carried the report, said it could not independently verify the claims. The report describes a web of companies in China and Singapore, centered on Shanghai Century Litong, that won preferred cloud-partner status within months of its June 2023 founding. When orders for export-restricted chips stalled, roughly 240,000 H100, H200 and A100 units allegedly reached China. Some of that capacity reportedly served Alibaba, Tencent and smaller Chinese AI labs. The company's board said a committee of independent directors with outside counsel is running the review. The board added that it has no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised.

From the November 6 close of $186.64, the two-day slide is 8.51%, roughly $383 billion of market value on about 24.1 billion shares. The GuruFocus profile is lopsided: GF Score 92/100, Profitability 10/10, Financial Strength 9/10 and Momentum 10/10, but GF Value Rank only 2/10. At $170.75 the shares trade 60.10% below the $427.93 GF Value, yet GuruFocus itself tags the setup "Possible Value Trap, Think Twice." The model gap alone is no bargain signal. The next hard test is the November 17 third-quarter report, where any export-control questions would surface in guidance or disclosures.
